about: The Profit Pool Drivers PRISM simulates: for each driver its scores, exposures and sources. scripts/generate_seed.py turns this file into prism/seed_drivers.py and data/driverCodeMap.ts; edit this file and re-run the generator, never the generated files. highest_numbers is the highest driver number each force has used: a new driver takes the next one and raises it, so no number is given to a second driver. Field meanings: docs/DRIVERS.md.

drivers.name: Private label structural penetration and premium own-label tiers (Europe)
drivers.mechanism: Price/mix (promo depth, price-gap compression); competitive capture by retailer brands
drivers.description: Private label reached a record 50% unit share and 42% value share (EUR 324bn) across Europe's six largest grocery markets (Circana, April 2026; Germany 52% units, 44% value); 34% of branded units are sold on promotion against 14% for private label. Momentum slowed in 2025 as national brands won shoppers back (Circana), but the 2026 energy-shock inflation can re-accelerate it. In HCB's core, German laundry private label is about 20% of value and cleaners about 30% (YouGov panel, MAT Mar 2026); hair private label is low. Private label now contributes significantly more to premium-tier growth in Western Europe than branded players (NIQ, June 2026: +514 against -170), through tiers such as Lidl Deluxe, dm Balea and Tesco Finest, which removes the quality rationale that protected mid-tier brand pricing.

sources.title: Circana: private label reaches record 50% unit share across EU6

drivers.name: GLP-1 adoption reshapes personal-care demand (appearance investment, GLP-1 hair shedding)
drivers.mechanism: Volume (new scalp/thinning and volumising occasions); mix (appearance investment)
drivers.description: 11% of US adults now take a GLP-1 for weight loss (3% in 2024, 8% in 2025; Gallup, July 2026) and 22-23% of US households contain a user; oral Wegovy passed 3m prescriptions in five months. Users cut grocery spend about 4% after a year and reallocate to self-care and appearance categories (Numerator, Circana). Hair-thinning demand is a documented side effect (JAAD cohorts 2025-26; Ulta CEO: 'hair loss with GLP-1s is real'; US prestige hair serums nearly +60% in H1 2026), although the clinical base rate is small. Europe is not 12-18 months behind but structurally lower (about 2% of adults; reimbursement limited), so this is a North-America-led driver for HCB's hair care, Olaplex and Not Your Mother's.

drivers.name: Hair-care premiumisation: prestige, professional and science-led tiers outgrow mass
drivers.mechanism: Price/mix (core); competitive capture (L'Oréal PPD, K18); channel (value migrates to specialty, salon-retail, e-commerce)
drivers.description: Premium hair keeps outgrowing mass: US prestige hair +11% in dollars and +8% in units in H1 2026 against mass +7% with units falling (Circana); L'Oréal Professional Products grew +7.5% like-for-like in 2025 (+15% in its premium hair segment, Kérastase double-digit) and +12.6% like-for-like in H1 2026; Unilever's K18 posted 'very strong double-digit growth'. Henkel management puts past hair-market growth at about 4.5% a year and expects premium hair to compound at about 5%; HCB Hair grew +4.2% organic in H1 2026 with strong consumer and very strong professional growth. With Olaplex (about EUR 370m of annual sales, closed 7 July 2026) HCB is now global number two in professional hair, so premiumisation is both a direct tailwind and an integration exposure (Olaplex has declined since its 2022 peak, Kline). Bond-building and biomimetic-peptide science (K18, Olaplex, Elvive Collagen Lifter, Dove Fibre Repair) is the reason-to-believe; clinical evidence at cosmetic concentrations is still thin.

drivers.name: Clinical-efficacy ('cleanical') premiumisation in hair and body
drivers.mechanism: Price/mix (efficacy-proven tiers); claim-substantiation cost carried by G-05/G-03
drivers.description: Proof beats positioning: L'Oréal Dermatological Beauty grew +11.3% and Professional Products +12.6% like-for-like in H1 2026 with hair care double-digit across divisions; US prestige hair serums rose nearly 60% and skincare 9% in H1 2026 (Circana); 56% of Western European shoppers require premium to prove features or performance and 63% link premium to high-quality ingredients (NIQ). The instrument that raises the substantiation bar is Directive (EU) 2024/825 (EmpCo), applying from 27 September 2026, not the stalled Green Claims Directive. HCB's fit improved with Olaplex (bond-building, clinical claims) and Gliss Scalp Balance; the counter-signal is European body care (Fa), where 'clean' without 'clinical' declined in H1 2026.

sources.title: NIQ: Premium has a new price in Western Europe FMCG

drivers.name: Ageing consumers: grey-coverage colour demand, gentle and scalp care for ageing hair (net of grey acceptance)
drivers.mechanism: Mix (colourants, gentle care, scalp/thinning); volume mixed sign in LHC
drivers.description: 22.0% of the EU population was 65 or older on 1 January 2025 (+2.9 pp in ten years) and the share keeps rising to mid-century; 34% of Germans over 65 live alone. For HCB the evidenced mechanisms are two: grey-coverage and grey-blending colour demand (Hair Colorants and Hair Styling made the strongest contributions to HCB consumer hair growth in H1 2026) and gentle, scalp and thinning care for ageing hair. The offset is real: the over-55s showed the largest increase in dupe buying between 2024 and 2026 (Circana), US salon colour was flat in 2024 (Kline) and L'Oréal calls the professional colour market 'more challenging'. Colourants are HCB's largest hair profit line, so the net effect is a modest expansion.

sources.title: Circana: Life imitates brands, how dupe demand is evolving
Kline via Happi: US professional salon hair care 2024

drivers.name: Cost-of-living squeeze, round two: energy-shock inflation, entrenched value-seeking and wallet shift to services
drivers.mechanism: Price/mix (promo depth, downsizing limits, trade-down); volume in discretionary personal care
drivers.description: The squeeze did not end with the 2024-25 rate cuts: after the Middle East war began in late February 2026, euro-area inflation returned to 3.3% in August 2026 (energy +14.3%) and the ECB raised rates on 11 June 2026 citing the war. BCG's June 2026 survey finds 53% of Europeans worried about daily finances (40% in 2024) and expects the pullback to persist even if conditions improve; McKinsey expects more than three-quarters of consumers worldwide to keep trading down. HCB's own Q2 2026 shows the new form of the squeeze: price -0.5%, volume +2.1%. Two constraints tighten it: FMCG shelf inflation is only 1.1% (NIQ EU5, 13 weeks to May 2026) against direct-material inflation in the high single digits, and shrinkflation-disclosure laws (France since July 2024, Italy since April 2025, Austria since April 2026; the Bremen court's Milka ruling of May 2026) remove covert downsizing as a lever. Retail's share of EU private consumption fell for a fourth year (31.9%) as wallets move to services and travel. Premium bifurcation holds: NIQ Premium+ is 28.2% of Western European FMCG value and growing 4.1%.

drivers.name: Scalp care (skinification of hair) becomes a regimen step across prestige and mass
drivers.mechanism: Price/mix (serums and treatments at 1.5-3x shampoo price points); volume (added regimen step)
drivers.description: US prestige scalp care grew 19% in H1 2025 and logged a third consecutive year of double-digit growth in 2025 (Circana); scalp-focused products and serums drove prestige hair in H1 2026. The segment is still small (3.4% of US salon retail, Kline) but every major now has a scalp flagship: Dove Scalp + Hair Therapy (US 2024, UK April 2026), Head & Shoulders and Vichy Dercos, and HCB launched Gliss Scalp Balance in February 2026 (five SKUs, EUR 5.99-8.99). The microbiome story is the ingredient layer under this driver, with a thin clinical base (three randomised trials indexed).

sources.title: Unilever H1 2026 results (Dove Scalp + Hair Therapy)

drivers.name: Hair-thinning demand medicalises: GLP-1 shedding, tele-derm Rx, supplements, cosmetic thickening (incl. men)
drivers.mechanism: Volume (thickening and anti-shedding regimens); mix (serums, ampoules); channel caveat (Rx and supplement tiers captured by tele-derm and Nutrafol)
drivers.description: Thinning has become a medical-adjacent category: JAAD cohorts (2025, 2026) document GLP-1-associated hair loss; Unilever is marketing Nutrafol 'as a complement to a GLP-1 regimen' to lift new-customer conversion; L'Oréal's Vichy Dercos and Redken Acidic Grow Full are growth drivers; Hims & Hers reached USD 2.35bn revenue in 2025 with hair loss one of its founding specialties (no hair split disclosed). The Rx and supplement tiers sit with telehealth and Nutrafol, which caps HCB's addressable slice to cosmetic thickening (Schwarzkopf, Gliss, BC Scalp Genesis). Men's scalp, thinning and grey-blending routines are the evidenced male-grooming slice for HCB (Men Perfect, Syoss Men); the broader men's market growth sits in skincare, fragrance and DTC, where HCB is absent.

drivers.name: Dupe economy and value-equivalence normalisation (all cohorts)
drivers.mechanism: Price/mix (willingness-to-pay ceiling for branded formulation collapses to the cheapest credible equivalent); capture by dupe brands
drivers.description: 58% of US shoppers have bought a dupe, 51% of beauty buyers have bought a beauty dupe (hair is 18% of those purchases) and 70% would buy a beauty dupe even if they could afford the original (Circana, August 2026). The fastest 2024-26 increase is among consumers over 55 and half of USD 100k+ households now buy dupes: this is an all-cohort value-equivalence norm, not a youth subculture. HCB is now exposed from both ends: mass 'the-dupe-is-us' plays (Gliss bond repair, Syoss) gain, while Olaplex (acquired July 2026) is one of the most duped prestige hair franchises.

sources.title: Circana: Life imitates brands, how dupe demand is evolving
The Fashion Law: MCoBeauty v Sol de Janeiro

drivers.name: China domestic-brand capture in beauty and hair (Douyin-native competition)
drivers.mechanism: Competitive capture by Douyin-native domestic brands; price compression below RMB 300
drivers.description: Domestic brands held 57.4% of China's RMB 1.1tn cosmetics market in 2025, the fifth consecutive year of gains (CAFFCI); 65% of sales are online and domestic brands are Douyin-native while foreign brands remain weighted to Tmall; several foreign brands withdrew or downsized in 2024-25. The mechanism is channel and price, not nationalism. HCB's China hair exposure is substantial (Vidal Sassoon Greater China acquired 2024, Schwarzkopf, Syoss, Shiseido Professional; a China hair-care and colourants plant expansion is in the 2026 capex list), yet Henkel's Asia-Pacific region grew 'very strong' organically in H1 2026, driven by Hair and P&G regained share in China after 15 quarters. The share shift is two-thirds done; what remains is a tail.

sources.title: Caixin citing CAFFCI: homegrown brands dominate China's beauty market
P&G Q4 FY2026 earnings call transcript

drivers.name: US Hispanic demographic dividend in hair and laundry, delayed by the 2025-27 enforcement and migration shock
drivers.mechanism: Volume (households, frequency); mix (premium scent, softener); near-term negative sub-scenario 2025-27
drivers.description: Hispanic Americans numbered 70.1m on 1 July 2025 (about 21% of the population) and delivered 76% of US population growth, but growth halved to +1.35m as net international migration fell 54% to 1.3m (Census Vintage 2025). Hispanic households over-index on hair care (index 138) and laundry care (126) (NIQ) and spend 41% more on laundry supplies (BLS), which is why HCB's US portfolio is exposed both ways. In 2025 Hispanic per-household spending growth slowed to 0.8% with unacculturated households -4.8% (Numerator); a 1% tax on cash and money-order remittances took effect in January 2026 and ICE removals exceeded 356,000 in FY2026 to July. Not Your Mother's (Curl Talk) partly closes the curl gap; HCB still has no Hispanic-targeted platform.

sources.title: US Census Bureau: population growth slows
Numerator: Hispanic household spending growth sharply decelerating
BBVA Research: Mexico 2026 begins with new remittance tax

drivers.name: Textured and curly hair as a mainstream category (North America first, then growth markets)
drivers.mechanism: Penetration and regimen depth (higher spend per head); mix; geographic (NA, Africa, LatAm, diaspora)
drivers.description: Curl care was the only US salon-retail segment that did not decline in 2024 (Kline); textured-hair consumers spend about 78% more on hair products (Syensqo, via BeautyMatter 2026); P&G (Mielle), Unilever (SheaMoisture), L'Oréal (Mizani, Garnier Curl Method 2025) have occupied the space. The category has no independent sizing. HCB now owns Not Your Mother's Curl Talk (26 SKUs, mass curl, North America) but has no type-4/coily or Africa-relevant range.

drivers.name: Sub-replacement fertility and population decline (developed-market volume erosion)
drivers.mechanism: Volume (fewer children, population decline after the 2029 EU peak)
drivers.description: EU total fertility fell to 1.34 in 2024 (lowest in the series), Japan at a new record low and Korea 0.80 in 2025 (Korea rising for a second year), US births -1% in 2025. The EU population peaks at 453m in 2029 (EUROPOP2025) and is only 1.5% lower by 2050; East Asia shrinks faster but is a small HCB exposure. EU average household size has been flat at 2.3 since 2014 (Germany 2.0 since 2009) and household counts still rise to 2035 (Germany 42.7m in 2025 to 43.2m, Destatis), so there is no household-count volume loss inside the horizon. Atomisation therefore raises loads per capita; the genuine headwinds are fewer children (fewer kid-related loads, lower soil) and post-2029 population decline, which compound mainly beyond the horizon.

drivers.name: Dishwasher penetration catch-up drives auto-dish consumption (Southern and Eastern Europe, Türkiye, MEA; China and India back-loaded)
drivers.mechanism: Volume (ADW occasions grow with the installed base); geographic mix
drivers.description: Germany has dishwashers in 77.3% of households (Destatis LWR 2024) and the US in 72.7% (EIA RECS 2020), while China is at about 3% (All View Cloud estimate cited by CHEAA) with volume growth of only about 2% a year and Euromonitor describes Brazil, India and Mexico as low-penetration or flat. For HCB the catch-up that matters is where Somat and Pril sit: Southern and Eastern Europe, Türkiye and MEA; Henkel reported very strong dishwashing growth in Q3 2025 and double-digit hand-dish growth in H1 2026. In India, China and Brazil HCB has no meaningful ADW franchise and Finish (Reckitt, now a refocused 'Powerbrand') absorbs most of the migration.

sources.title: Destatis: Ausstattung privater Haushalte mit Haushaltsgeräten
Reckitt: completes divestment of Essential Home

drivers.name: Scent-led premiumisation of laundry additives and finishers (boosters, laundry perfumes, fragranced variants)
drivers.mechanism: Price/mix (additives at 3-10x the per-load value of detergent); competitive capture (P&G leads, Henkel follows)
drivers.description: Scent boosters and laundry perfumes have graduated from novelty to a structural premium segment: the only public series sizes the global booster market at EUR 1.9bn in 2023 heading to EUR 3bn by 2028 (Euromonitor, cited by Unilever), with fragrance boosters growing more than 21% outside the US in the year to Q1 2024 (GMI, cited by Unilever); Circana's 2025 Pacesetters include a Downy scent booster and Downy Unstopables Unlimited is a 2026 Rising Star. Henkel's Fabric Care grew double-digit in Q3 2025 and 'significantly' in Q1 and Q2 2026 while Fabric Cleaning declined, and Silan launched its first liquid laundry perfume in Austria in September 2025 (EUR 4.99). P&G's Lenor/Downy Unstopables franchise leads. Risk inside the pool: the EU microplastics restriction bans non-degradable fragrance encapsulates from 17 October 2029 (Henkel already markets Silan perfumes as microplastic-free).

sources.title: Unilever: the fabric enhancer market is changing
P&G citing Circana New Product Pacesetters 2025
Henkel Austria: Silan Selection Floral Essences

drivers.name: Garment care beyond cleaning: specialty care, fibre renewal and refresh occasions (synthetic wardrobes, short and cold cycles, longevity norms)
drivers.mechanism: Price/mix (specialty care at a multiple of heavy-duty per-load value); volume (care and refresh occasions added to the wash)
drivers.description: Polyester was 59% of global fibre output in 2024 (Textile Exchange) and synthetic wardrobes, short and cold cycles and the demand for sophisticated fragrance are the shifts Unilever names as reshaping fabric enhancers. Henkel's own reporting confirms the occasion: Fabric Care (Perwoll's category) grew double-digit in Q3 2025 and significantly in Q1 and Q2 2026 while Fabric Cleaning declined; Perwoll's range is built on a fibre-renewal platform. The between-wash refresh occasion is real but unquantified (Febreze is an air-care brand that passed USD 1bn in 2011, not a fabric-refresh business). EU textile policy (the ban on destroying unsold textiles for large enterprises from 19 July 2026, the textile EPR directive adopted in 2025) regulates apparel, not detergents; it acts only as a slow awareness driver for longevity norms. Woolite moved to PE ownership (Vestacy) in December 2025 and is a watch item.

drivers.name: US immigration reversal slows household formation (North American volume headwind)
drivers.mechanism: Volume (household counts in laundry, dish and body care)
drivers.description: US net international migration fell from 2.7m (2024) to 1.3m (2025) with 0.3m projected for 2026; household formation by recent immigrants is projected to drop from 640,000 (2024) to about 143,000 by 2027, pulling total household growth down to the Joint Center's low series of 690,000 a year (Harvard JCHS, August 2026). Young-adult headship fell to 32.7% in 2024. Household counts drive volume in HCB's North American laundry (all, Persil, Snuggle), dish and Dial body care.

drivers.name: Mass hair and body unit decline: value migrates to prestige, specialty and e-commerce
drivers.mechanism: Volume (mass shelf units); channel (specialty, salon-retail, e-commerce set the terms)
drivers.description: US mass hair grew +7% in dollars in H1 2026 with units down, while prestige hair grew +11% with units +8% and prestige body care +16% (Circana); mass hair was 'among the softer performers' in 2025 with growth from value combo packs. Kline records e-commerce gaining 15.6 points of hair-care sales over 2019-24 while salon back bar and take-home both lost share. HCB's hair is still majority mass in Europe (Schwarzkopf consumer, Syoss, Gliss, Taft) where private label and discounters compound the unit erosion, and European body care (Fa) declined in H1 2026. C-03 models the premium upside; this line carries the mass-shelf loss, as PRISM's one-sided driver grammar requires.

sources.title: GCI Magazine (Kline/Circana data): hair care 2025, scalp health and category blur

drivers.name: Growth-market currency depreciation and hyperinflation haircut on euro gross profit (Türkiye, Egypt, other IMEA and LatAm currencies)
drivers.mechanism: Geographic mix in euro terms; COGS (dollar-priced feedstocks bought by lira and pound subsidiaries); IAS 29 monetary losses
drivers.description: IMEA grew +12.1% organically in 2025 and +14.9% in H1 2026, yet nominal sales fell 6.7% and were flat, and IMEA adjusted EBIT went from EUR 213m (2024) to EUR 200m (2025) and EUR 111m in H1 2026 at a 10.4% margin against 18.9% in Europe (Henkel AR 2025, H1 2026 report). Türkiye is consolidated under IAS 29 with a EUR 39m monetary loss in 2025; the lira lost 20.6% on average in 2025 and a further 9.8% by September 2026; Turkish inflation is 31.8% and Egyptian 14.9% (July 2026). Consumer Brands' H1 2026 nominal sales carried a -4.1 point FX effect, and Henkel guides a low-single-digit negative translation effect for 2026. Without this haircut the model converts organic growth-market percentages one-for-one into euro gross profit, which overstates the euro effect by roughly half on the evidence of the last six quarters.

sources.title: Henkel Annual Report 2025 (regional table p. 350; IAS 29 note p. 355)
Henkel Half-Year Financial Report 2026 (regional table p. 32)

drivers.name: Growth-market expansion (IMEA and India led; SEA, LatAm-Mexico, SSA as sub-exposures), stated in organic terms
drivers.mechanism: Geographic mix; penetration; price recovery (with C-36 carrying the FX haircut)
drivers.description: IMEA delivered organic growth of +12.1% (2025), +12.8% (Q1 2026) and +17.4% (Q2 2026) with both Laundry & Home Care and Hair contributing; Consumer Brands in Asia-Pacific grew very strongly in H1 2026, driven by Hair (Vidal Sassoon Greater China, a China hair plant expansion in the 2026 capex list). India's beauty and personal care market is USD 23bn growing about 12% a year to USD 40bn by 2030 (Redseer) but HCB's Indian footprint is hair-only and sub-scale until the Pril and Fa licences to Jyothy Labs ended on 31 May 2026; washing-machine penetration is about 20%. Southeast Asia's digital economy passed USD 300bn of GMV with video commerce at 25% of e-commerce (e-Conomy SEA 2025), but HCB there is professional-hair led. Latin America is Mexico-anchored for HCB; Mexico's record FDI is dominated by reinvested earnings rather than new plants and USMCA was not renewed at the July 2026 review, so no nearshoring volume enters this driver. In Sub-Saharan Africa NIQ sizes the five largest measured markets at about USD 74bn, with Nigeria's 54% growth being 5% volume. AfCFTA's phase-down for sensitive goods only began on 1 January 2026 and actual trade has so far run through the Guided Trade Initiative: a watch item. Middle East watch item: Gulf consumption has been affected since the war began (L'Oréal), with Saudi Arabia resilient; Indonesia's halal mandate for cosmetics bites 17 October 2026.

sources.title: Redseer: India BPC to USD 40bn by 2030
Business Standard: Henkel ends Pril and Fa licences with Jyothy Labs
World Bank: Sub-Saharan Africa's growth holds but downside risks mount

drivers.name: Discount channel share gain in Europe and the US (Aldi, Lidl; variety discounters as price-floor channels)
drivers.mechanism: Channel margin and terms (lower trade margin, PL-led format); price/mix (the discounter reference price caps the category ladder)
drivers.description: Discounters hold 46.6% of German food-retail revenue (EHI, 2024 data) and remain Europe's fastest-growing physical channel outside Germany: Lidl grew 6.1% to EUR 140bn in FY2025, Aldi Nord grew 7.4% group-wide to about EUR 31bn (5.1% in Germany), Lidl GB reached a record 8.4% UK share in April 2026, and IGD sees discount growing 4.8% a year to 2030. In Germany itself the gain plateaued in 2025 (Edeka, Rewe and Lidl grew 2.7-3.6%; Aldi Süd +1.2%). Aldi US is adding 180+ stores in 2026 towards 3,200 by 2028 and claims one in three US households. Variety discounters (Action, Tedi, Woolworth) took 23% more non-food spend in two years (GfK) and set the visible price floor for branded hair and detergent packs. The pool mechanism is trade-margin dilution and price-ladder compression, not delisting.

Aldi US: doubles down on growth in 2026

drivers.name: E-commerce and marketplace share gain at lower brand net margin (incl. auto-replenishment lock-in and club packs)
drivers.mechanism: Channel margin and terms (marketplace fees, fulfilment, price transparency; subscription defaults fix share at the moment of subscription)
drivers.description: The channel is not mature in the US: Walmart US e-commerce grew +24% in the quarter to July 2026 and Amazon's net sales +20% in Q2 2026, while Schwarz Group's online revenue was flat at EUR 1.7bn in FY2025 (continental Europe is maturing, Germany's FMCG online share stays low single digits). Amazon's Alexa for Shopping (May 2026) adds Scheduled Actions (recurring purchases) and Buy for Me; auto-replenishment programmes fix share at the moment of subscription, which is why default status matters more than consideration share in laundry and auto-dish. Amazon is number one in online beauty in eight of ten European countries (NIQ), the entry ramp for every Asian and social-native hair challenger. Loyalty scheme facts have moved: Rewe left Payback in December 2024, Edeka joined in January 2025. Club and big-pack channels in North America (Kirkland Signature about a third of Costco sales) carry lower unit margin and the strongest US private-label vehicle.

sources.title: WWD (NIQ data): Amazon conquers online beauty in Europe

drivers.name: European retailer buyer-power concentration: alliances, M&A and cross-border sourcing
drivers.mechanism: Channel margin and terms (alliance-level negotiation drives pan-European price harmonisation towards the lowest national price; listing and promo fees)
drivers.description: Edeka and Rewe alone hold 46.8% of German grocery and the trade press calls the power relations between the big four 'cemented' (NIQ Trade Dimensions data, 2025); buying alliances are re-forming rather than fading (Concordis: Carrefour and Coopérative U negotiating with multinational suppliers from 2026; Eurelec with E.Leclerc, Rewe and Ahold Delhaize sourcing jointly since 2025, Ahold Delhaize citing 'price differences between European countries that cannot be objectively explained'); consolidation continues (Carrefour exits Italy and Romania, 165 Auchan supermarkets rebannered to Intermarché from October 2026, Aldi US converting Southeastern Grocers). The EU Single Market Strategy (May 2025) commits to tackle territorial supply constraints, the legal lever alliances need to buy cross-border; until a proposal is tabled it stays a watch item inside this line.

sources.title: Lebensmittel Praxis (NIQ Trade Dimensions): Top 30 LEH 2025
Retail Insight Network: Carrefour and Coopérative U form Concordis
IGD: Europe roundup M&A, growth and regulation

drivers.name: Social commerce (TikTok Shop) becomes a scaled beauty channel (hair only; live commerce a minority format in the West)
drivers.mechanism: Volume (new occasions and impulse in styling, colour, bond-repair care); margin caveat (platform commission plus 10-20% affiliate fees)
drivers.description: TikTok Shop's US GMV reached USD 15.1bn in 2025 (+68%) and USD 11.8bn in H1 2026 (+103%), global GMV is on track to pass USD 100bn in 2026 (Momentum Works); beauty and personal care is the largest category (USD 2.08bn in the US in H1 2026, the number-three beauty e-commerce channel, Circana). In Europe the four continental markets did about EUR 500m of estimated GMV in the 90 days to 9 July 2026 (Kalodata via Lengow; Germany EUR 175m) and ten markets are live since June 2026; NIQ ranks it among the top online beauty retailers in the UK, Germany, Italy, France, Spain, Ireland and the US. The US divestiture risk cleared with the January 2026 joint venture. It is not a 'top-5 FMCG channel': a low single-digit share of e-commerce in the US and France. Livestreaming is a minority of Western GMV (Momentum Works puts US Live at about 8% of attributed GMV in H1 2026 against about 51% for the Shop tab); the Douyin live model matters in China and Southeast Asia.

drivers.name: Professional and bond-repair hair brands cross into retail and e-commerce, lifting the hair-care price ladder
drivers.mechanism: Price/mix (professional and bond-repair brands lift the retail price ladder); competitive capture caveat (led by L'Oréal PPD, Olaplex, K18, Wella)
drivers.description: L'Oréal Professional Products grew +7.5% like-for-like in 2025 (first time above EUR 5bn, a record 27% share of the professional market, Kérastase double-digit) and +12.6% like-for-like in H1 2026, with 39% of the division's sales already outside salons. Henkel Hair grew +4.2% organically in H1 2026 with strong consumer and very strong professional growth, and now owns Olaplex, the archetype of salon-to-retail crossover. Ceteris paribus the crossover raises category value but is led by competitors, so this line carries the price-ladder mechanism and X-18 carries the professional-channel contraction side.

The real exposures are solid opacifiers and other polymer microparticles in LHC liquids (2028) and fragrance encapsulates (2029), which land on the scent-premium pool (C-28); Henkel states it has replaced synthetic encapsulates in Europe and is still seeking a fully biodegradable opacifier.

drivers.name: EU carbon-cost pass-through: ETS around EUR 80/t, ETS2 from 2028, CBAM definitive 2026 and downstream metal goods 2028
drivers.mechanism: COGS via energy, logistics fuel (ETS2) and metal packaging pass-through; free-allocation phase-out 2026-34
drivers.description: CBAM's definitive regime started 1 January 2026 (authorised declarants above 50 tonnes a year; scope cement, steel, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity, hydrogen); the Commission's December 2025 proposal (COM(2025) 989) extends it from 1 January 2028 to steel- and aluminium-intensive downstream products (the Annex I list), not to surfactants or formulated products; the Council agreed its position on 12 June 2026. ETS2 for buildings and road-transport fuels becomes fully operational in 2028; EUAs traded around EUR 80/t in July 2026 and the CBAM certificate price was EUR 75/t for Q2 2026. CSRD Scope 3 disclosure is a reporting duty, not a cost mechanism.

drivers.name: Structural European energy-price disadvantage (electricity about 2x, gas 3-6x US) plus the 2026 gas shock and the erosion of the European chemical supply base
drivers.mechanism: COGS for European-manufactured volume (energy is a low-single-digit share of conversion cost) and via European supplier costs and concentration
drivers.description: IEA: EU electricity prices for energy-intensive industries in 2025 were 'on average roughly double the prices in the United States' and more than 50% above China and India; European gas averaged USD 11.96/mmbtu in 2025 against USD 3.53 in the US (3.4x) and USD 18.06 against USD 2.89 in July 2026 (6.2x) after the Hormuz closure (World Bank). The gap widened in 2026 rather than narrowing. The consequence is upstream: 37 Mt or about 9% of European chemical capacity closed in 2022-25 at six times the pre-2022 rate (Cefic), thinning European sources of surfactant intermediates and packaging resins and raising import dependence; Kearney's 2026 index shows US manufacturing imports at a four-year high despite tariffs, so 'nearshoring' is not visible in the data. Climate adaptation is a watch item: Munich Re puts European nat-cat losses in 2025 at USD 11bn against a USD 35bn ten-year average.

drivers.name: Oil-derived feedstock, packaging-resin and freight cost shock from the 2026 Middle East war (surfactants, ethoxylates, PET/HDPE/PP, transport)
drivers.mechanism: COGS (the petro-feedstock half of HCB's raw-material bill: LAS and alcohol ethoxylates for laundry liquids, bottle and cap resins, solvents, propellants; freight)
drivers.description: Global oil supply crashed by 10.1 mb/d in March 2026 after attacks on energy infrastructure and the near-total disruption of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz; Brent rose about 65% in the month, its highest monthly rise ever, and the World Bank projects energy prices +24% in 2026 with Brent averaging USD 86 before falling to USD 70 in 2027. Building-block chemical prices spiked at the fastest pace in almost 20 years (European polypropylene spot +40% in two weeks, ICIS). Henkel raised its 2026 direct-material guidance from a low single-digit to a high single-digit increase (May 2026, confirmed in August), citing 'geopolitical tensions in the Middle East', and the CFO said H2 'will be hit much harder'; P&G guides a USD 1bn after-tax raw-material, energy and transport headwind for FY2027; Unilever's gross margin fell 70 bps. Under ceteris paribus this COGS increase is unrecovered; any pricing recovery is a management lever outside the simulation. China's ethylene and paraxylene overcapacity is the post-2028 downside-price branch.
